t: Under a Jewellers Block policy, loss of jewellery whilst being sent by registered insured post or by angadia/courier is covered under:
e: Section I covers property in premises, Section II covers property in custody of the insured/employees/agents outside premises, Section III covers transit by registered post/courier, Section IV covers fixtures and fittings.

t: On transfer of ownership of an insured vehicle, the transferee must apply to the insurer for transfer of the policy in his name within:
e: Under GR 17 of the erstwhile tariff the transferee has 14 days from transfer to apply; the TP cover is deemed transferred in the meantime under Section 157 of the MV Act.

t: Loss proximately caused by delay, even though the delay is caused by an insured peril, is:
o: Covered under all three sets of clauses
e: The delay exclusion is common to all Institute Cargo Clauses; marine policies cover physical loss or damage, not loss of market due to delay.

t: Under the Institute War Clauses (Cargo), the 'waterborne agreement' limits war risk cover to the period the goods are on the overseas vessel and for a period after arrival at the final port of discharge of:
e: War risks on cargo attach when loaded on the vessel and end on discharge or 15 days after arrival at the final port, whichever is earlier.

t: Under the no-fault liability provision (Section 164) of the MV Act, the claimant:
o: Is not required to plead or establish wrongful act, neglect or default of the vehicle owner
Must prove negligence of the driver beyond doubt
Can claim only if the vehicle was uninsured
Cannot claim if he contributed to the accident
e: No-fault compensation is payable without proof of negligence; the claimant may alternatively pursue a fault-based claim under Section 166 for a higher amount.

t: Which of the following is an in-built peril under the Bharat Griha Raksha policy but only an add-on cover under the SFSP policy?
e: BGR includes acts of terrorism as a standard insured event, whereas SFSP covers terrorism only through the terrorism add-on at additional premium.

t: Before claiming a constructive total loss under a marine policy, the insured must:
o: Tender a notice of abandonment to the insurer
Wait for 12 months from the casualty
e: To treat a loss as CTL the insured must give notice of abandonment; failing this, the loss is treated only as a partial loss.

t: A private car with an ex-showroom price of Rs 10 lakh is 4 years and 6 months old at renewal. Under the IDV depreciation schedule, its IDV will be:
e: For vehicles exceeding 4 years but not exceeding 5 years the depreciation is 50%, giving an IDV of Rs 5 lakh.

t: A Third Party Administrator (TPA) in health insurance:
o: Underwrites health risks on behalf of the insurer
Decides the premium rates for health products
Is licensed by IRDAI to provide health services such as cashless facilitation and claims processing on behalf of insurers
Bears the claim liability jointly with the insurer
e: TPAs provide administrative and network services for a fee; the risk and the final liability remain with the insurer.

t: Which section of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes third party insurance compulsory for a vehicle used in a public place?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 146 provides that no person shall use a motor vehicle in a public place unless a policy complying with Chapter XI is in force.

t: Under an Erection All Risks policy, the testing and commissioning period for second-hand (used) machinery is:
e: Testing of used/second-hand machinery is excluded under EAR; for new machinery a testing period (typically 4 weeks) is included.

t: The part of a policy document that contains the insurer's undertaking to indemnify the insured against the specified perils, subject to terms, is called the:
e: The operative (or insuring) clause states what the insurer promises to pay; the recital identifies the parties and the attestation is the signature clause.

t: Which of the following is typically excluded under a Directors' and Officers' Liability policy?
o: Loss arising from dishonest or fraudulent acts of the director, once established
Defence costs for a regulatory investigation
Claims by employees for wrongful termination
e: D&O covers wrongful acts in a managerial capacity; deliberate fraud, dishonesty and personal profit to which the director was not entitled are excluded once finally adjudicated.

t: A health policy has a 20% co-payment on all claims. The admissible hospitalisation expenses are Rs 1,00,000. The insurer pays:
e: Co-payment is the percentage of each admissible claim borne by the insured; 20% of Rs 1 lakh is borne by the insured, so Rs 80,000 is paid.

t: The 'material damage proviso' in a Consequential Loss (Fire) policy means that:
o: The CL sum insured cannot exceed the fire sum insured
The CL claim is payable only if there is a fire policy covering the insured's property
A CL claim is admissible only if a claim for the damage has been admitted under the material damage (fire) policy
Material damage must exceed Rs 1 lakh
e: The proviso links the CL cover to the material damage cover: unless liability for the property damage is admitted under the fire policy, the CL claim does not arise.

t: Occupations such as builders, contractors, engineers engaged in superintending field work, veterinary doctors and drivers are classified for PA rating under:
e: Group I is administrative/sedentary occupations; Group II covers moderate manual or field work; Group III covers hazardous occupations.

t: A warehouse worth Rs 40 lakh is insured for Rs 30 lakh with Insurer A and Rs 10 lakh with Insurer B, both policies containing the contribution condition. A loss of Rs 8 lakh occurs. Insurer B pays:
e: Each insurer pays in the ratio of its sum insured to the total: B pays 10/40 x Rs 8 lakh = Rs 2 lakh and A pays Rs 6 lakh.

t: Material fact, for the purpose of the duty of disclosure in a proposal form, is best defined as a fact which:
o: Is already known to the insurer
Would influence the judgement of a prudent underwriter in deciding whether to accept the risk and at what terms
Relates only to previous claims history
e: The test is objective: whether a prudent insurer would regard the fact as relevant to acceptance or rating, not what the proposer thinks.

t: Under IRDAI regulations, a surveyor appointed to assess a loss must submit the survey report to the insurer within how many days of appointment (unless an extension is granted)?
e: The surveyor must submit the report within 30 days of appointment; in exceptional cases the insurer may allow an extension up to a further period as specified.

t: A consignment is insured under a marine cargo policy at CIF value Rs 10 lakh plus 10%. Goods are totally lost at sea. The insurer pays:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Marine cargo policies are valued policies; in a total loss the agreed insured value (CIF + 10% = Rs 11 lakh) is payable irrespective of actual market value.

t: Which perils under the SFSP policy may be deleted at inception at the option of the insured, with a corresponding reduction in premium?
e: Storm, tempest, flood, inundation (STFI) and riot, strike, malicious damage (RSMD) are the two peril groups that can be opted out of; the others are mandatory.

t: A 'floating' Fidelity Guarantee policy is one which:
o: Provides a single sum insured covering a specified group of employees, any one or more of whom may cause the loss
Automatically covers all new employees without declaration
Follows the employee to a new employer
e: Floating (floater) FG covers a group of named employees for an aggregate amount, whereas individual and collective policies carry separate limits per person.

t: The indemnity period under a Consequential Loss (Fire) policy commences from:
o: The date the material damage claim is admitted
The date of reopening of the business
The date the policy is renewed
e: The indemnity period runs from the date of damage for the number of months selected, during which business results are affected.

t: As per IRDAI's 2024 health insurance norms, the maximum entry age ceiling (earlier 65 years) for offering health insurance policies has been:
o: Removed, so that insurers must offer products to all age groups
Kept at 65 years for indemnity products
e: The 65-year entry age cap was withdrawn; insurers are expected to design products for all ages including senior citizens.

t: Under a hull policy the 3/4ths collision liability (running down clause) covers part of the shipowner's liability to the other vessel. The remaining one-fourth and liabilities such as crew injury and oil pollution are usually covered by:
o: The shipowner's Protection and Indemnity (P&I) club
e: P&I clubs provide mutual cover for the shipowner's third party liabilities not covered by the H&M policy, including the balance 1/4th collision liability.

t: A factory building valued at Rs 80 lakh is insured for Rs 60 lakh under an SFSP policy with the average condition. Fire damage is assessed at Rs 20 lakh. The claim payable is:
e: Claim = Loss x Sum Insured / Value at risk = 20 x 60/80 = Rs 15 lakh; the insured bears the balance as his own insurer.

t: Under the IRDAI framework (Section 64UM read with the Surveyors Regulations), appointment of a licensed surveyor is mandatory for claims other than motor where the estimated loss exceeds:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The threshold is Rs 50,000 for motor claims and Rs 1 lakh for other claims; below these limits the insurer may assess the loss in-house.

t: Which of the following is covered under a Boiler and Pressure Plant insurance policy?
o: Wear and tear of boiler tubes
Damage from failure of individual tubes
Explosion or collapse of the boiler including flue gas explosion, with damage to surrounding property and third party liability
e: The policy covers explosion/collapse (including flue gas explosion) of the boiler, surrounding property damage and TP liability; wear and tear, tube failure and overload tests are excluded.

t: A vessel worth Rs 8 crore carries cargo of shipper A valued at Rs 1 crore and shipper B valued at Rs 1 crore. To save the vessel, cargo worth Rs 50 lakh is jettisoned as a general average sacrifice. Shipper A's general average contribution (based on contributing values) is:
e: Total contributing value = 8 + 1 + 1 = Rs 10 crore; A's share = 1/10 of Rs 50 lakh = Rs 5 lakh, recoverable from A's cargo insurer.

t: An insured earned 45% No Claim Bonus and then made an own damage claim during the year. The NCB applicable at the next renewal will be:
e: Under the Indian motor NCB rules a single claim wipes out the entire accumulated NCB; it does not step down by one level.

t: A pre-acceptance risk inspection (survey) of an industrial fire risk is carried out mainly to:
o: Assess the physical hazard and recommend rates, terms and risk improvements
Determine the moral hazard of the proposer
Fix the amount of the surveyor's fee for future claims
e: Risk inspection evaluates construction, occupancy, protection and exposure features so the underwriter can rate and impose warranties; it does not assess moral hazard.

t: Under a Personal Accident policy, the cumulative bonus for each claim-free year of renewal is commonly:
o: No cumulative bonus is given in PA
e: Many PA policies increase the CSI by 5% per claim-free year up to a maximum of 50%, applicable to death and permanent disablement benefits.

t: An insurer has a 5-line surplus treaty with a retention of Rs 10 lakh per risk. It accepts a risk with a sum insured of Rs 90 lakh. The amount it must place outside the treaty (e.g. facultatively) is:
e: Treaty capacity = 5 lines x Rs 10 lakh = Rs 50 lakh; with retention Rs 10 lakh the total automatic capacity is Rs 60 lakh, leaving Rs 30 lakh to be placed facultatively.

t: ECGC Ltd functions under the administrative control of:
e: ECGC is a Government of India enterprise under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, though its insurance business is regulated by IRDAI.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

t: A Deterioration of Stock (in cold storage) policy pays for:
o: Theft of stock from the cold storage
Deterioration of stock due to rise in temperature caused by breakdown of the refrigeration machinery insured under an MBD policy
Deterioration due to shortage of stock
Loss of market value of the stock
e: DOS cover is granted only in conjunction with MBD on the refrigeration plant and responds when a covered breakdown causes temperature variation spoiling the stock.

t: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, an employer is NOT liable to pay compensation where the injury (not resulting in death or permanent total disablement) is directly attributable to:
o: The employee having been under the influence of drink or drugs at the time
e: The Act excludes liability for injuries caused by the employee's intoxication, wilful disobedience of safety rules or wilful removal of safety guards, except where death or PTD results.

t: Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 deals with:
o: Duty of the insurer to satisfy judgments
Requirements of policies and limits of liability
Compensation on the structured formula basis
e: Section 146 mandates insurance, Section 147 lays down what a policy must cover and the limits, Section 149 deals with satisfying awards, and Section 165 constitutes MACTs.

t: A 'cash loss' settlement in a motor own damage claim is one where:
o: The insurer pays the IDV and takes the salvage
The insurer pays the assessed repair cost (after depreciation and excess) without the vehicle being repaired, as agreed with the insured
The insurer pays only the labour component
The repairer is paid directly in cash
e: In cash loss the insured chooses not to repair or repairs elsewhere; the surveyor's assessment net of deductions is paid and the insurer is discharged.

t: The Insurance Information Bureau of India (IIB) was set up by IRDAI primarily to:
o: Act as a central data repository and analytics body for the insurance industry
Underwrite large industrial risks on behalf of PSU insurers
e: IIB, promoted by IRDAI in 2009, collects and analyses industry data (e.g. motor vehicle and health claims data) and is not a risk carrier or regulator.

t: A policy carries a franchise of Rs 10,000. If a loss of Rs 12,000 occurs, the insurer pays:
e: Under a franchise, once the loss exceeds the franchise amount the entire loss is paid; losses below the franchise are not paid at all.

t: A Public Liability policy has an AOA limit of Rs 1 crore with an AOA:AOY ratio of 1:3. Two accidents in the year give rise to admissible claims of Rs 80 lakh and Rs 1.5 crore respectively. The total amount payable by the insurer is:
e: First claim Rs 80 lakh is within AOA; second is capped at AOA Rs 1 crore; total Rs 1.8 crore is within the AOY of Rs 3 crore.

t: In health insurance, 'migration' means:
o: Shifting the policy to a different insurer
Moving from one health product to another product of the same insurer with continuity benefits
Transferring the policy to a family member
Changing the TPA servicing the policy
e: Portability is movement between insurers; migration is movement between products or plans within the same insurer, both with credit for waiting periods served.

t: Post-harvest losses under PMFBY are covered for crops kept in 'cut and spread' condition in the field for a maximum period of:
o: Up to the end of the season
e: Post-harvest cover is for a maximum of two weeks (14 days) from harvesting against cyclone, cyclonic rains and unseasonal rains.

t: The 'agreed bank clause' attached to a fire policy on hypothecated stocks provides that:
o: The bank must pay the premium
The policy cannot be cancelled by the insurer
The bank is liable for the first 10% of any loss
Any claim payable is paid to the bank and its receipt is a full discharge to the insurer
e: The clause protects the financing bank by making loss payable to it, and provides that the bank's interest is not prejudiced by acts of the insured.

t: A 'first loss' burglary policy is one in which:
o: The insurer pays only the first claim in the year
Theft by the first intruder only is covered
The policy covers only the first Rs 10,000 of a loss
The sum insured is fixed at a percentage of the total stock value, as the whole stock is unlikely to be stolen in one event, and average does not apply up to that amount
e: First loss policies suit bulky stocks; premium is charged on the first loss sum with a loading on the balance value, and the full value must be declared.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: In reinsurance terminology, 'retention' means:
o: The portion of a risk or loss the ceding insurer keeps for its own account
The commission paid by the reinsurer to the cedant
The reinsurer's maximum liability under a treaty
The premium reserve withheld from the reinsurer
e: Retention (or net line) is what the cedant retains net of reinsurance, fixed with reference to its capital and risk appetite.

t: A duty insurance policy on imported cargo pays a claim:
o: On every loss irrespective of whether duty has been paid
Only if the insured proves the goods were sold at a profit
Only if customs duty has actually been paid on goods that arrive damaged or lost after landing
Together with the marine policy in all cases as a single sum
e: Duty cover protects the importer who must pay duty on damaged goods; no claim arises if the goods are lost before duty becomes payable or if duty is refunded.

t: The limit of indemnity under a compulsory policy taken under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 must be:
o: Not less than the paid-up capital of the undertaking, subject to a maximum of Rs 50 crore
Equal to the turnover of the undertaking
e: The Act requires the policy to be for an amount not less than the paid-up capital and not more than Rs 50 crore.
